study_identification_part.si_4_title: Alzheimer's disease heterogeneity revealed by neuroanatomical normative modeling

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: The reference cohort (n=33,072) was compiled from nine publicly available datasets listed in Supplementary Table 1: ABCD, Cam-CAN, CNP, FCON, HCP, OASIS-3, PNC, TOP, and UK Biobank. The normative model was previously trained on this reference cohort under a prior study (Verdi et al.). The adaptation dataset (n=20) consisted of cognitively normal older adults scanned at Imperial College Healthcare NHS Trust (ICHT), categorized as SINGLE-SITE. The clinical cohort (n=86) was drawn from the Imperial Amyloid PET Cohort (Imperial APC), a real-world clinical cohort at ICHT.

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: The normative model was previously trained on the reference cohort (n=33,072) compiled from nine public datasets. The adaptation dataset (n=20 CN adults at ICHT) was used to recalibrate (transfer learning) the pre-trained model to the local acquisition site. The Imperial APC clinical cohort (n=86 amyloid-positive AD patients) was used for clinical application, generating individual z-scores and outlier maps.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "Hierarchical Bayesian regression was previously trained on the reference cohort (compiled by Kia and colleagues) consisting of a large sample of healthy controls..."; "This model was then optimized using cortical thickness data from controls scanned at the same acquisition site as the clinical cohort (n = 20). This gives stable estimates of the transferred model parameters in an adapted transfer learning approach. This recalibrated model was then used to generate regional cortical thickness z-scores for each participant in the clinical cohort..."

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: A single normative model of cortical thickness was used. The reference cohort of 33,072 cognitively normal adults was used for training (pre-trained under Kia et al. / Verdi et al.). The paper does not distinguish train/test splits within the reference cohort; the full 33,072 was described as the training reference. An additional adaptation dataset of 20 CN adults was used for transfer learning recalibration but is not counted as part of the normative model training cohort per se.

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: The reference cohort age statistics (mean, sd, median) are not reported in this paper. The reference cohort was compiled in a prior study (Verdi et al., refs 20/24), with details referred to as 'see Table S1 for cohort details.' Supplementary Table S1 only partially renders, showing ABCD dataset age range 9-11. The remaining dataset rows are not visible due to formatting issues. The minimum age of at least 9 years can be inferred from the ABCD dataset (age range 9-11). The paper notes '17,586 (53.2%) participants were aged between 49 and 87 years, which was the age range in the clinical cohort,' indicating the cohort spans well beyond that range (younger participants from ABCD, PNC, HCP, etc.), but the overall max age is not explicitly stated.
